cross_cutting_mbo_finding: G23's Monday says something the block's other days cannot: THE MOVE AND THE LIQUIDITY WERE IN DIFFERENT PLACES, AND THE DEEP TAPE WAS INERT. On 0713 the overnight phase carried 5,269 of the session's 85,744 lots - 6.1% of the volume - and delivered -170 of the -250 phase-summed session move, 68% of it. The two deep phases carried 93.9% of the volume and delivered -80. Add the -360 gap and the picture is stark: 85.5% of the -620 day-move was priced in the seam and the thin overnight, on 6% of the day's traded volume, and the entire liquid US session moved the market -80. The block's impact-coefficient break lands inside this day: k3 (final-phase price change per unit final-phase aggressor lot) ran 0.302 on 0710 and 0.026 on my 0713 - an order of magnitude - so 1,162 lots of net aggressive SELLING in my final phase bought -30 USD. The generalizable form: when a book's marginal impact has collapsed, the session cannot express information at all, and a seam-Monday's entire informational content is therefore transacted in the two windows where the book is thinnest - the gap and the reopen drift. A specialist forecasting the SESSION on such a day is forecasting the wrong object. This also inverts the standing catch-up-window grammar in a specific, testable way: my window (06-10 ET) did adjudicate the weekend - it made an 08:06 high +90 above the open, then sold 740 USD into the 10:30 low - but it adjudicated on -158 lots of net flow across 53,859, i.e. it drifted to a verdict rather than transacting one. A flowless verdict from the catch-up window is not a weak version of a ratify; it is the market declining to price the weekend information at all, which on this day was the bearish answer.

gap_vs_session_split.session_derivation: Three steps. (1) CLASS from the leg's own realized decay, per E's item-4 operating rule (never the declared-degraded vol_regime): the leg's three sessions into my day ran -530, -2,050, -660 - a decaying continuation after the -2,050 shock. (2) COEFFICIENT routes within the class: the measured final-phase impact coefficient had already halved into my day (0708 k3 0.557 -> 0710 k3 0.302), so whatever flow arrives converts to less price than it did last week. That argues the middle-to-low end and, more importantly, argues that the session's move will be DRIFT rather than DELIVERY. (3) LOCALIZATION: if the move is drift rather than delivery, it lives in the thin phase, and the thin phase on a seam Monday is the reopen overnight - which makes the session an extension of the gap rather than an independent object. p50 -250, band -400..0. The realized decomposition confirms all three steps: -170 of the -250 landed in the 5,269-lot overnight, and the 80,475 lots of deep US session produced -80.
gap_vs_session_split.which_question_the_coefficient_answers: The run directive asks whether the collapsed coefficient explains the session, leaving the gap as the separate question. The collapsed coefficient explains phases 2 and 3 - 93.9% of the volume, 32% of the session move, 80 USD - completely and quantitatively: -158 net flow bought -50, and -1,162 net flow bought -30. It does not explain phase 1, which is 68% of the session move. So the day has TWO separate questions, not one: (i) the SEAM object = gap -360 plus overnight -170 = -530 on 6.1% of the volume, which is where all the information was transacted; and (ii) the DEEP-SESSION object = -80 on 93.9% of the volume, which the collapsed coefficient fully explains and which carried no information at all.
